question: Does the fixed recent-batch refit that beat H-LLM on the new four nine-channel arrays improve the whole gas stream when substituted for the project's frozen observer? Decide whether to add a fixed tool, comparing it to the previously registered source-plus-site logistic refit and current observer.
frozen_before_transfer: Reuse the five recorded streams from feedback-refit-transfer.json. Official public, UCI late, one-year, SGP40 B and C are development transfer checks; no new scores are claimed as unknown hardware. Same previous-batch IDs selected with seed 17, same label clock, features, order and budget. Retain every device and every target class regardless of the first outcome.
operation: At deployment use the current observer. After each batch except the last fit one RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=1,random_state=0,n_jobs=1) on just that batch's returned labels. Source-only medians cover genuine missing features, all-empty source columns excluded. A single-class feedback batch is legitimate and produces a single-class tree. Use it on the next batch without hindsight or thresholds. A second arm replaces the native vote with this tree and updates the same calibrated voting bank on actually issued votes. The two arms share the fit. Zero paid calls.
controls_and_gate: Reproduce reference observer and fixed source-plus-site logistic scores from their archived blind batch receipts on identical row IDs and feedback; compare per-run pooled Macro-F1, worst-class recall and actual fit count. Only recommend universal use if at least 0.01 Macro-F1 over each of both controls on all five and worst recall loss no greater than 0.02. Otherwise keep current default. Treat any site-dependent result as exploratory until tested on fresh first-use data.
